newsitem.title: USA: U.S. outlaws computer-generated child pornography.
newsitem.headline: U.S. outlaws computer-generated child pornography.

text.p: Congress cracked down on child pornographers in a new law that took effect on Tuesday making it illegal to use computer technology to appear to depict children in sexual situations.
Such depictions of children, produced by computers without using children, have been outside the scope of federal law.

"While federal law has failed to keep pace with technology, the purveyors of child pornography have been right on line with it. Passage of this bill will help to correct that problem," said Judiciary Committee chairman Orrin Hatch, a Utah Republican.

The bill did not address new or expanded regulations of the Internet. The Justice Department has asked the Supreme Court to overturn a landmark ruling by a Philadelphia appeals court which blocked as unconstitutional a new federal law barring indecency on the Internet.

Hatch said the Judiciary Committee determined that computer-generated pornography poses many of the same dangers to children as does pornography made from unretouched photographs, in that it can be used to seduce children into sexual activity or to encourage a pedophile to prey upon children.

The new law sets mandatory prison sentences of 15 years for production of child pornography, 5 years for possession of the materials and life in prison for repeat offenders convicted of sexual abuse of a minor.

The child pornography law was included in part of a broad spending bill President Clinton signed into law on Monday. It had passed the Senate on Monday just hours before the midnight deadline for the start of the new financial year.

Computers can be used to alter sexually explicit photographs, films and videos so as to produce materials virtually indistinguishable from unretouched photographs. But the new materials make it difficult to win convictions because it can be impossible for prosecutors to identify individuals or to prove that the materials were produced using children.
The new law would allow prosecution of pornographers whether or not the identity of the child could be determined.
It defined as child pornography any image -- photograph, video, computer-generated image that depicts or appears to depict a minor engaged in sexually explicit conduct.
